source_text: Excoriant holocaustum et divident illud membratim; filii Aaron ignem et ligna et membra divisa imponunt. Vitulus — Christus; corium litterae detractum spiritalem sensum aperit. Membratim dividere — ordinare profectus: incipientibus, proficientibus, perfectis aptare doctrinam. Ligna altaris — usque ad lignum passio carnis; ignis desursum divinitatis. Interanea et pedes aqua lavantur — baptismi sacramentum.
thought_title: The flayed calf: the letter stripped away reveals the spiritual sense
orientation: Origen is explaining the burnt offering ritual from Leviticus, showing how each action points to Christ and the soul's progress.
pass_a_gloss: They flay [the] holocaust and they will divide it limb by limb; [the] sons of Aaron [the] fire and [the] wood and [the] divided limbs [upon it] place. [The] calf — Christ; [the] skin of [the] letter [having been] drawn off [the] spiritual sense opens. Limb by limb to divide — to arrange [the] advances: for [the] beginning, for [the] advancing, for [the] perfect to fit [the] teaching. [The] wood of [the] altar — as far as [the] wood [the] passion of [the] flesh; [the] fire from above of [the] divinity. [The] entrails and [the] feet [with] water are washed — [the] sacrament of baptism.

lemmas.gloss: limb by limb, piece by piece

choices.why: The verb excoriare means to strip the skin; 'flay' keeps the physical action vivid, which Origen immediately interprets spiritually.

choices.english: the skin of the letter stripped away
choices.why: Corium is the hide or skin; Origen uses it as a metaphor for the literal sense covering the spiritual sense. 'Skin' preserves the physical image.
rejected: the covering of the letter removed
the hide of the letter taken off

choices.why: Aperit means opens or reveals; 'opens' keeps the sense of unveiling what was hidden under the skin.
Profectus is progress or advancement; Origen is describing the ordered stages of spiritual growth. 'Progress' captures the developmental sense.
rejected: to set in order the growth

choices.why: Usque ad means 'as far as, even to'; lignum is wood, referring to the cross. The phrase points to Christ's passion extending to the wood of the cross.

choices.english: the fire from above of the divinity
choices.why: Desursum means 'from above'; the fire represents divine nature. The genitive divinitatis is kept as 'of the divinity' to preserve the source's compactness.
rejected: the fire from on high of the Godhead

pass_b_english: They flay the burnt offering and divide it limb by limb; the sons of Aaron place the fire, the wood, and the divided pieces upon the altar. The calf is Christ; the skin of the letter stripped away opens the spiritual sense. To divide it limb by limb is to arrange the progress: to fit the teaching to beginners, to those advancing, and to the perfect. The wood of the altar is the passion of the flesh, even to the wood of the cross; the fire from above is the divinity. The entrails and the feet are washed with water: this is the sacrament of baptism.
